paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Peter followed at a distance, sat down by the fire, and then denied Jesus three times when people connected him to Him (Luke 22:54-60). I think this one hurts, because Peter is the same man who got close to Jesus and heard His warning. Nobody gets to watch Peter and feel superior, because we all know what it's like to go quiet when it costs us something.

Now look at what happens next. The rooster crows, and "the Lord turned and looked at Peter" (Luke 22:61). I don't think that look is a door slamming. I think it's the Lord reaching Peter right in the middle of his worst moment. Peter remembers the word he was given, goes outside, and "wept bitterly" (Luke 22:62). Tears like that tell me he knew exactly what he'd done, and that's the first step back, friend.

Then the story swings to Jesus, who stays steady while men mock Him and a council tries to corner Him. He tells them, "from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God" (Luke 22:69). Peter let go in the courtyard, but Jesus held on all the way through. So when you stumble, baker, don't hide at a distance. Look up, because the Lord who sees you is still the One who is seated in power, and this story isn't over.
